description: How to turn an analysis into a pipeline that anyone can rerun and trust: command-line tooling, workflow engines, containers, cluster and cloud execution, provenance, large file formats and automated tests. Students build a malaria-genome surveillance style pipeline step by step, run it at scale on simulated cluster and cloud resources, and prove that a second run reproduces the first.
modelledOn: Wilson et al., Good Enough Practices in Scientific Computing
Koster and Rahmann, Snakemake: a scalable bioinformatics workflow engine
Wilkinson et al., The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
Docker and OCI image specification documentation
outcomes: Compose shell tools and scripts to process large text and tabular files in streaming fashion, safely and in parallel.
Express an analysis as a dependency graph in a workflow engine with parameters, retries and resumable execution.
Package a pipeline environment in a container and pin all versions so that a rebuild reproduces the same result.
Run workflows on a batch scheduler and on cloud resources, sizing resources and estimating speed-up and cost.
Record provenance and metadata so that a dataset meets FAIR principles, and verify reproduction using checksums.
Choose file formats and indexes for large data, and test and release a pipeline with automated continuous integration.

units.title: Command-line tools at scale
topics: Shell fundamentals: pipes, redirection, exit codes, quoting and globbing
Text-stream tools for tabular and sequence files: grep, sed, awk, cut, sort, uniq and join
Robust shell scripts: strict mode, functions, argument parsing and static checking
Parallelism in the shell: background jobs, xargs -P and GNU parallel
Streaming versus loading into memory; I/O-bound versus CPU-bound work and measuring with time

units.title: Project structure and environments
topics: Version control for analysis projects: branches, tags and handling large data files
Project layout, configuration files and parameter separation
Environment and dependency management: virtual environments, lock files and version pinning
Reusable code: packaging, command-line entry points and logging

units.title: Workflow engines and dependency graphs
topics: Dependency graphs and incremental builds with make-style rules
Rule-based workflow engines: wildcards, targets, config and sample sheets
Dataflow workflow engines: channels, processes and scatter-gather
Portable workflow descriptions: tool wrappers and common standards
Failure handling: retries, checkpoints, idempotent steps and resuming runs
Design patterns and a case study: a malaria parasite genome surveillance pipeline

units.title: Containers for reproducible environments
topics: Images, layers, Dockerfiles and the build cache
Reproducible builds: pinned versions, base-image choice, image digests and multi-stage builds
Containers inside pipelines: bind mounts, user permissions and rootless runtimes on clusters
Registries, software bills of materials and vulnerability scanning
Environment capture compared: container images versus package-manager environments

units.title: Cluster scheduling and cloud execution
topics: Batch schedulers: queues, partitions, job scripts, job arrays and dependencies
Resource requests, fair-share and backfill scheduling; measuring CPU and memory efficiency
Shared file systems versus object storage; data locality and staging
Cloud execution: virtual machines, spot capacity and autoscaling batch pools
Cloud storage, access control and cost per sample
Scaling out: speed-up, Amdahl's law and bottleneck analysis

units.title: Provenance, metadata and FAIR data
topics: Provenance: what was run, on what input, by whom, and the PROV model
Metadata standards, controlled vocabularies and schema validation of sample sheets
The FAIR principles: persistent identifiers, licences, access and reuse
Data management plans, consent and data sovereignty in African genomics projects
Checksums, immutable data and content addressing to verify reproduction

units.title: Large file formats and indexing
topics: Sequence and variant formats: FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM/CRAM, VCF and GFF; block compression
Indexing for random access: tabix-style indexes, BAM indexes, Bloom filters and k-mer indexes
Columnar and chunked array formats: Parquet, Arrow, HDF5 and Zarr
Sorting, merging and external-memory processing of files larger than memory
Compression trade-offs: gzip, zstd and reference-based compression
Validating and converting formats inside a pipeline

units.title: Testing, continuous integration and release
topics: Unit tests for pipeline scripts and small test datasets
Regression and end-to-end tests: golden outputs and tolerance for numerical drift
Continuous integration for pipelines: triggers, caching and matrix builds
Monitoring, logging and failure reports for long runs
Capstone: release an end-to-end reproducible pipeline with documentation and a verified second run

schedule.title: The shell as a data tool
schedule.exercise: Count variants per chromosome in a VCF-like file with a pipeline of grep, cut, sort and uniq, then wrap it in a script that fails safely on bad input.

tasks.title: Use pipes and redirection to count lines, unique values and the most common ID in a tab-separated sample file, and check the counts
Use awk and sort to compute per-sample mean read depth from a table and join it with a sample sheet by ID
Write a bash script with strict mode and argument checks that filters a FASTQ file by length, and test it with bad inputs

schedule.title: Parallel and streaming processing
schedule.exercise: Process 24 sample files in parallel with a bounded number of workers, measure the speed-up and explain why it stops growing.

tasks.title: Run a counting command over 20 files with xargs -P at 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers and record the elapsed time of each
Compare a streaming pipeline with one that loads a large file into memory and report time and peak memory for each
Write a Python generator that streams a large FASTQ file, computes GC content per read and compares memory use with a list-based version

schedule.title: Project structure and environments
schedule.exercise: Set up a repository for an analysis with configuration, pinned dependencies, a command-line entry point and a tag marking the version used for a report.

tasks.title: Create a repository, commit a script and a small data file, ignore large outputs, and tag a release you can return to
Create a virtual environment, install pinned package versions, freeze them to a lock file, and rebuild the environment elsewhere
Turn an analysis script into a command-line tool with arguments, logging levels and a config file, and run it on two datasets

schedule.title: Dependency graphs and rule-based workflows
schedule.exercise: Write the dependency graph for a three-step read-filter-count pipeline, run it incrementally after changing one file, and show which steps rerun.

tasks.title: Write a Makefile for a three-step pipeline, run it, change one input and show that only the downstream steps rerun
Write a small rule-based engine that expands wildcards over a sample sheet, builds the DAG and prints the execution order
Implement scatter-gather over 8 chunks of a file with a merge step and verify the merged output equals the unsplit result

schedule.title: Portable workflows, failure and patterns
schedule.exercise: Take a pipeline that fails halfway, add retries and checkpoints so it resumes, and map it to a portable description.

tasks.title: Make three pipeline steps idempotent and add a resume mode that skips completed steps after a forced failure in step two
Describe a tool wrapper for a read aligner with inputs, outputs, parameters and container image, and draw the workflow graph
Build a pipeline from reads to a variant count table for 6 samples, injecting a failing sample, and show the run completes for the others

schedule.title: Containers for reproducible environments
schedule.exercise: Write a Dockerfile for the pipeline with pinned versions, rebuild it, and show that the output checksum is identical across two builds.

tasks.title: Write a Dockerfile for a small analysis script, build it, run it and show how a layer is reused when only the script changes
Pin the base image by digest and package versions, build twice, and compare the output checksums of the two containers
Run the container with a mounted data directory as a non-root user and fix the file permission errors in the outputs

schedule.title: Batch schedulers and job scripts
schedule.exercise: Write a job array script for 30 samples with memory and time requests, and compare job efficiency for two resource settings.

tasks.title: Write a job array style script that runs 20 sample jobs with a bounded number in flight and a dependent merge job
Schedule a mix of long and short jobs with first-come and backfill policies in the scheduler visualiser and compare waiting times
Compare staging data once to local disk against reading from shared storage in a simulation of 50 jobs, reporting total I/O time

schedule.title: Cloud execution and scaling
schedule.exercise: Run the pipeline on a pool of cloud workers, estimate the cost per sample, and find the Amdahl limit on speed-up for your workflow.

tasks.title: Launch an autoscaling worker pool, submit 100 tasks, and record the number of workers and the finishing time as load changes
Store input in a bucket with read-only access for workers and write-only for results, then report storage and compute cost per sample
Measure speed-up at 1 to 32 workers with a 10 percent serial fraction, fit Amdahl's law and name the bottleneck

schedule.title: Provenance, FAIR and reproduction
schedule.exercise: Add provenance and metadata to a finished run, publish it with an identifier and licence in a mock repository, and verify an independent rerun by checksum.

tasks.title: Compute checksums of all pipeline outputs, store them in a manifest, rerun and verify that every file matches
Validate a sample sheet against a schema with required fields and controlled vocabularies and report every error with its row
Decide in a scenario how to share genome data collected from patients across a regional network, scored on consent, sovereignty and reuse

schedule.title: Sequence formats and indexes
schedule.exercise: Inspect FASTQ, SAM and VCF records by hand, build an index for random access to a sorted file, and compare row and columnar storage.

tasks.title: Extract the fields of five SAM records with cut and awk, decode the flag bits, and count mapped and unmapped reads
Build a byte-offset index on a sorted variant file and retrieve a genomic region without scanning the whole file
Store a 1 million row table as CSV and in a columnar format, and compare size and query time for a single-column filter

schedule.title: Large data, compression and conversion
schedule.exercise: Sort and merge a file larger than memory using chunks, choose a compression format for archive versus working data, and add validation to conversion.

tasks.title: Sort a large file by splitting into sorted chunks and merging them, and check the result with sort -c
Compress a sequence file with two compressors at three levels and chart size against time to pick one for archive and one for working storage
Convert a table between formats with a validation step that stops on an invalid record and reports its position and the reason

schedule.title: Testing and continuous integration
schedule.exercise: Write unit and end-to-end tests for the pipeline using a tiny test dataset, and configure continuous integration that runs them on every change.

tasks.title: Write unit tests for a read-trimming function covering empty, short and boundary-length reads, and run them to a pass
Create a golden output for a small dataset and an end-to-end test that compares a new run with a numerical tolerance
Add a continuous integration configuration that runs tests and the container build on a branch, and trigger a failing and a passing run

schedule.title: Monitoring, release and capstone
schedule.exercise: Release the pipeline with documentation, a changelog, a container and a verified second run on a fresh environment, and present the reproducibility evidence.

tasks.title: Add structured logging and a failure report to the pipeline, run it with an injected bad sample, and read the cause from the report
Clone the repository to a clean directory, rebuild the container, run the pipeline and verify the output checksums against the manifest
Run the released pipeline on a clean cloud environment with a fresh bucket and compare cost, time and outputs with your local run
